Legs.Subject: QuadraticExtensionField64.Multiply — five reduced base-field products with the square of the root folded back to the non-square (QuadraticExtensionField64.cs:148-157), at the three lean ladder primes 7, 1_000_003 and 2^61 − 1
Legs.Against: Oracles.PrimeFieldPolynomialProduct at tail [p − d, 0] — SCHOOLBOOK multiplication into a three-coefficient wide array followed by top-down reduction against the monic tail, in BigInteger. No closed pair formula anywhere on the reference side, and its own remark states no Montgomery form, no Barrett reduction, no field descriptor (Oracles.cs:1618-1619). Both sides EXACT, so condition (B) drops out entirely — there is no rounding substrate to share — and what agreement pins is purely the reduction policy

Legs.Subject: QuadraticExtensionField64.Add, Subtract and Negate — coordinate-wise through PrimeField64's three conditional folds
Legs.Against: the unbounded BigInteger sum, difference and negation reduced ONCE by ((x % p) + p) % p, inline in Subjects.ExtensionRingExact. The reference never branches where the subject's carrier forces it to: PrimeField64.Add tests sum >= Modulus, Subtract tests left >= right, Negate special-cases zero. Exact on both sides, so (B) is vacuous

Legs.Subject: QuadraticExtensionField64.FromBase as the ring embedding of F_p
Legs.Against: the BigInteger base sum and base product of the two lifted coordinates, inline in the same claim — the lift of a sum is the sum of the lifts and likewise for products, with both base values re-formed in arbitrary width rather than through PrimeField64

Legs.Subject: the Element positional constructor and its two readers round-trip at every swept pair BEFORE anything else reads them, and the product's two coordinates are compared against the polynomial reference's coefficient 0 and coefficient 1 SEPARATELY — the two are computed by different formulas, so a swapped constructor argument or a swapped reader reddens the multiply comparison rather than cancelling

the ring axioms the type declares: Zero is (0, 0) and a two-sided additive identity, One is (1, 0) and a two-sided multiplicative identity, Negate is the additive inverse, and Subtract(x, y) equals Add(x, Negate(y)) at every swept pair

ENVELOPE: the operand fold Subjects.ExtensionResidue reduces every sampled raw into [0, p) before it reaches the type, so this law says NOTHING about the unreduced-operand behaviour the members' docs decline to guard. ENVELOPE: at p = 7 the twenty-four committed edge raws collapse onto seven residues, so the small end of the ladder is degenerate by construction and the 61-bit entry is where the edge battery actually spreads
QuadraticExtensionField64.Norm — the closed form A² − d·B² as three separate reduced base products and one conditional-fold subtraction (QuadraticExtensionField64.cs:166-170)
Legs.Against: Oracles.QuadraticExtensionConjugateProduct — the element times its own conjugate, reduced as a POLYNOMIAL modulo t² − d through Oracles.PrimeFieldPolynomialProduct. A different derivation, not a transcription of the closed form; exact on both sides, so (B) is vacuous

Legs.Subject: the conjugate product's ROOT coordinate vanishes at every swept element of every ladder prime — the fact that makes the norm a base-field quantity at all, ASSERTED by the claim rather than assumed by the reference, which returns both coefficients
QuadraticExtensionField64.Norm's MULTIPLICATIVITY — N(x·y) against N(x)·N(y)
Legs.Against: the unbounded BigInteger product of the two reference norms reduced once, inline in Subjects.ExtensionNormTraceFrobeniusExact. This is EXACT at every element of every ladder prime with no sublattice fold anywhere — the deliberate contrast with the fixed-point family, where Laws.NormMultiplicativity needs Domain.SublatticeShift so its products do not round (LawRegistry.cs:40, Domains.cs:299)

Legs.Subject: QuadraticExtensionField64.Trace
Legs.Against: (2a) mod p formed unbounded in BigInteger and reduced once, inline in the same claim. The RULE is a single doubling on both sides and there is no second derivation of it; what this leg buys is the reduction policy — the subject's conditional fold sum >= Modulus against the reference's unbounded double and one remainder — and it says so rather than claiming more

Legs.Subject: QuadraticExtensionField64.Frobenius
Legs.Against: the pair (a, (p − b) mod p) formed in BigInteger, inline in the same claim — the conjugate reached without the subject's PrimeField64.Negate branch

Legs.Subject: the CHARACTERISTIC EQUATION: Multiply(x, x) equals Subtract(Multiply(FromBase(Trace(x)), x), FromBase(Norm(x))) at every swept element. Trace and Norm are the coefficients of x's own quadratic over F_p, which is a statement about the two TOGETHER that neither one's own reference makes
the defining equations of the conjugation: Multiply(x, Frobenius(x)) equals FromBase(Norm(x)) and Add(x, Frobenius(x)) equals FromBase(Trace(x))

Frobenius is an INVOLUTION and its fixed set is EXACTLY the base field: Frobenius(Frobenius(x)) == x everywhere, and Frobenius(x) == x if and only if x.B is zero. The 'exactly' half holds because p is odd, so b and −b differ for every non-zero b — the one place this family's characteristic enters a statement, and the half that catches a Frobenius that is the identity map
Frobenius is a ring AUTOMORPHISM on the swept pair: it carries sums to sums and products to products
ENVELOPE: as in extension-field.ring-vs-oracle, the operand fold reduces every raw before it reaches the type and the small ladder primes are degenerate under the edge battery

QuadraticExtensionField64.Inverse — the conjugate divided by the norm, whose one base-field inversion is PrimeField64.Inverse = value^(p − 2) run in ScaledResidueRing64's Montgomery form (QuadraticExtensionField64.cs:136-143, PrimeField64.cs:382-386)
Legs.Against: Oracles.ModularInverse of the reference norm by the EXTENDED EUCLIDEAN algorithm, lifted to the pair (a·n⁻¹ mod p, (p − b·n⁻¹) mod p) in BigInteger. Euclid is a different THEOREM from Fermat and the reference never enters Montgomery form, so neither the algorithm nor the representation is shared. Exact on both sides — (B) is vacuous

Legs.Subject: the round trip: Multiply(x, Inverse(x)) is One at every swept non-zero element of every lean ladder prime, which is the statement a wrong norm and a wrong conjugate cannot both survive
Inverse is an INVOLUTION — Inverse(Inverse(x)) == x — and it fixes One

the refusal: Inverse(Zero) throws DivideByZeroException, raised by PrimeField64.Inverse through the vanishing norm. ENVELOPE: in a genuine field Zero is the ONLY element whose norm vanishes, so the throwing arm is reached by exactly one operand — which the claim body visits explicitly on every iteration whatever the domain drew, rather than waiting for the sweep to supply it

ENVELOPE: the operand fold reduces every raw before it reaches the type, and the swept element is replaced by One where the fold lands on Zero, so the VALUE statement runs over every other element and the zero case is the refusal above

QuadraticExtensionField64.Pow over the exponent ladder 0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 255 at the SMALLEST lean prime — square-and-multiply walked LEAST-significant-bit first over a running power (QuadraticExtensionField64.cs:176-189)
Legs.Against: Oracles.QuadraticExtensionPower — MOST-significant-bit-first binary exponentiation whose multiplication step is Oracles.PrimeFieldPolynomialProduct. Two independences at once: a different schedule visiting different intermediates in a different order, and a different product step with no closed pair formula in it. Exact on both sides

Legs.Subject: QuadraticExtensionField64.Pow at the exponent p itself, at all three lean primes — sixty-one extension squarings at the top of the ladder, the deepest chain the type reaches in this suite
Legs.Against: the pair (a, (p − b) mod p) formed in BigInteger: the p-power map IS the conjugation, because d is a non-square and so d^((p − 1)/2) is −1. The reference is the theorem's value computed in arbitrary width, NOT the subject's own Frobenius, so a wrong Frobenius cannot move it

Legs.Subject: QuadraticExtensionField64.Pow at the exponent p + 1, a 62-bit exponent at the top of the ladder
Legs.Against: the lifted reference norm — Oracles.QuadraticExtensionConjugateProduct's first coordinate, with a zero root part — in BigInteger: x^(p+1) = x·x^p = x·conj(x) = N(x). It holds at the zero element too, so this leg needs no exclusion

Legs.Subject: the group order: Pow(x, p² − 1) is One at every swept non-zero element of every LADDER PRIME BELOW 2³², the order of F_{p²}'s multiplicative group. ENVELOPE: p² − 1 leaves ulong above 2³², so the 61-bit ladder entry is pinned by the p-power and (p + 1)-power legs instead of by this one — stated rather than left as a silent gap
the exponent poles the doc names: Pow(x, 0) is One for EVERY x including Zero, Pow(x, 1) is x, and Pow(Zero, e) is Zero at a non-zero ladder exponent
Pow at the exponents 0 through 8
Legs.Against: the same number of iterated Multiply calls on the same element
Legs.Shared: QuadraticExtensionField64.Multiply — the IDENTICAL member on both sides, so this leg pins the SCHEDULE and never the product. Both sides exact, so condition (B) is vacuous: there is no rounding substrate to share
Legs.Citation: the product itself is pinned classically by extension-field.ring-vs-oracle and extension-field.product-vs-oracle, and by leg 1 of this same case on the same swept operands

Legs.Subject: QuadraticExtensionField64.BatchInverse — the running-product method, one extension inversion turning the whole product over and a backward pass peeling each element off (QuadraticExtensionField64.cs:87-119)
Legs.Against: Oracles.ModularInverse of each element's own reference norm by the extended Euclidean algorithm, lifted to the conjugate-over-norm pair in BigInteger — element by element, with no running product anywhere. A completely different algorithm, exact on both sides

Legs.Subject: the in-place round trip: Multiply(values[i], original[i]) is One for every i of every batch, so a peel-off that mixed two positions is caught POSITIONALLY rather than only in aggregate
BatchInverse at length one
Legs.Shared: QuadraticExtensionField64.Inverse — the IDENTICAL member, which BatchInverse calls once on its running product. Exact on both sides, so (B) is vacuous
Legs.Citation: Inverse is pinned classically by extension-field.inverse-vs-oracle, and leg 1 of this case pins BatchInverse's own answers against Euclid at every length

Legs.Subject: BOTH scratch paths are reached: the batch-length ladder runs 1, 2, 3, 511 and 512 through the stack-allocated arm and 513 and 600 through the pooled one. ENVELOPE: the pooling itself is not observable through the public surface, so this pins the ANSWERS on both arms and never the rent-and-return

the refusal is ATOMIC — a batch carrying Zero throws DivideByZeroException and leaves EVERY element of the span byte-identical to what it held on entry, because the forward pass writes only the private prefix scratch. No XML doc states this; it is new evidence rather than a doc gap
an EMPTY span returns without throwing and without writing, which the early return at QuadraticExtensionField64.cs:90 is the whole of

ENVELOPE: this case consumes no operand domain and advances no frontier counter. Its statement is quantified over batch LENGTHS rather than over an operand stream, so the batch contents come from one seeded house Pcg32XshRr — the same shape Subjects.PrimeExtensionTwinsMonogenic uses. The ELEMENT-level arithmetic is what the swept cases own

QuadraticExtensionField64.SmallestNonSquare — the ascending walk on PrimeField64.LegendreCharacter, which decides the character by exponentiation in ScaledResidueRing64's Montgomery form (QuadraticExtensionField64.cs:60-66, PrimeField64.cs:391-397)
Legs.Against: Oracles.SmallestQuadraticNonResidue over Oracles.PrimeFieldCharacter — Euler's criterion by BigInteger.ModPow in PLAIN residues, at all thirteen ladder primes, under a declared step budget whose exhaustion is a named failure rather than a spin. Exact on both sides, so (B) is vacuous; what the leg pins is the character decision and the walk together

Legs.Subject: SmallestNonSquare at all thirteen ladder primes
Legs.Against: the Subjects.ExtensionPrime ladder's own declared second field — 2, 2, 3, 2, 2, 5, 3, 3, 2, 3, 11, 3, 3 at the moduli 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 97, 257, 65537, 1000003, 998244353, 2013265921, 2147483647 and 2^61 − 1
Legs.Citation: hand-derived from quadratic reciprocity and the supplementary law that 2 is a residue exactly at p ≡ ±1 (mod 8); the derivation for every entry is written out in the campaign spec. Deliberately a SECOND reference beside leg 1: the table is what a reference wrong in the same way as the subject would still have to agree with, and a wrong table fails the case rather than passing it. The failure message says which way to correct — where the Euler-criterion reference agrees with the subject, the TABLE is what is wrong

Legs.Subject: the MINIMALITY the member's name claims
Legs.Against: Oracles.PrimeFieldCharacter at every candidate strictly between two and the returned value — each must be a residue, never a non-residue — and BigInteger.ModPow of the returned value at (p − 1)/2 must be exactly p − 1 rather than merely not one. Without this leg the walk could return any non-residue at all and still pass leg 1, and a composite modulus could reach the character undetected

Legs.Subject: CreateCanonical is Create over the smallest non-square: its NonSquare equals the ladder's declared value, its BaseField equals the field it was handed, and the whole record equals Create(field, that value). CreateCanonical bypasses Create's guard by calling the private constructor (QuadraticExtensionField64.cs:54-55), so that it lands on the same object is a statement rather than a wiring fact
Create's ACCEPT/REFUSE decision, exhaustively over every reduced value in [1, p) at the six ladder primes at or below 97 and over a fixed square ladder plus the declared non-square above them
Legs.Against: Oracles.PrimeFieldCharacter: Create must throw ArgumentException naming the parameter nonSquare exactly where the character is +1, and must succeed with NonSquare and BaseField reading back verbatim exactly where it is −1. The case fails on a wrong REFUSAL as readily as on a wrong acceptance

Legs.Subject: Create REFUSES the literal zero with ArgumentException naming nonSquare, at every ladder prime — the arm LegendreCharacter's own zero short-circuit is the whole of, and the one value where the folding described in the reduced-generator row below does not apply

the REDUCED-GENERATOR bound, enforced ahead of the character test and stated at every ladder prime: the modulus itself, twice the modulus, the modulus plus the declared non-square, and ulong.MaxValue are each refused with ArgumentOutOfRangeException naming nonSquare. The modulus row is the one with teeth — LegendreCharacter folds an unreduced argument through ScaledResidueRing64.Encode and reports the resulting zero power as −1 rather than 0 (PrimeField64.cs:391-397), so the character alone would ADMIT p and hand back F_p[t]/(t²), the dual numbers. The other rows are what keep record equality meaning 'the supplied reduced generator agrees': d and d + p can no longer become two unequal descriptors of one extension. This statement REPLACES the doc gap that pinned the old acceptance

the DEFINING field invariant, by exhaustion at the ladder primes 3, 5, 7, 11 and 13 and over EVERY generator Create accepts at each: only the zero element has a vanishing Norm, every non-zero element has one, and Multiply(element, Inverse(element)) is One. This is precisely the statement the admitted-modulus quotient failed — its non-zero surd (0, 1) had norm zero and no inverse — so it is what the bound above is worth, measured rather than argued. ENVELOPE: quadratic in the modulus and run once per accepted generator, so it stops at 13; the primes above it are covered by the accept/refuse decision and by this family's arithmetic cases, which never reach a descriptor the bound would have caught

every factory names the DESCRIPTOR when it was handed one that names no field: Create, CreateCanonical and SmallestNonSquare each refuse a default-initialized baseField with ArgumentException naming 'baseField', ahead of any generator work. Without it the reduced bound would compare against a zero modulus and blame nonSquare for a base-field mistake

the DEFAULT EXTENSION is its own descriptor rather than a wrapper the base field's guard happens to cover, and it is stated separately: One, Zero, Add, Subtract, Negate, Multiply, Inverse, Pow, Norm, Trace, Frobenius, FromBase and BatchInverse at length zero and length three all refuse with InvalidOperationException, at `default` and at an unassigned array element alike, each row named in the failure text. Without the extension's own guard, coordinate addition and negation would inherit unreduced base-field arithmetic while the product and inverse paths failed incidentally on a zero modulus — the same split the prime field carried. BaseField and NonSquare stay outside the policy and read the uninitialized state, which is what this case asserts equality against — and PRINTABILITY is asserted on ToString itself: a hand-written PrintMembers prints the base field and the non-square alone, so a default value formats as its raw state, nested default base field included, instead of throwing from a guarded identity with the failure misattributed to the PRIME field whose One prints first in the synthesized walk

extension identity: two extensions are equal exactly when both the base field and the non-square agree — equal at the same pair, unequal at two distinct non-squares of one prime (3 and 5 over F_7, whose residues are 1, 2 and 4), and unequal at one non-square SHARED by two primes (6, the least value outside the residues of both F_7 and F_11; 3 will not serve, because it is 5² modulo eleven and Create rightly refuses it there)

ENVELOPE: this case consumes no operand domain and advances no frontier counter — its statement is quantified over the declared prime ladder and, at or below 97, over each field's whole residue set, which is exhaustion rather than sampling

QuadraticExtensionField64.Multiply at the 61-bit ladder prime 2⁶¹ − 1, over the house FOUR-OPERAND edge battery — every element component drawn from the committed edge set independently, which the width-2 lane stream in extension-field.ring-vs-oracle does not do
Legs.Against: Oracles.PrimeFieldPolynomialProduct at tail [p − d, 0] — the same shared-nothing schoolbook route. Exact on both sides, so (B) drops out

Legs.Subject: the raw carriage is lossless in BOTH directions: every reduced component is below PrimeField64.MaximumModulus = 2⁶², so Subjects.ExtensionResidue lands inside the non-negative longs the BinaryElemOp shape carries and the returned coordinates cast back without wrapping. No sign or width policy sits between the law and the kernel

ENVELOPE: this law's edge battery runs at ONE modulus — the 61-bit one, where the base products actually fill the UInt128 reduction and where the edge set spreads across the most residues. The other ladder entries are swept by extension-field.ring-vs-oracle instead, on its own key
